q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on other scientific research is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 5425 - Capital Outlay on Other Scientific Research
options.C: 4810 - Capital Outlay on New and Renewable Energy

e: Major Head 5425 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Other Scientific Research, mirroring revenue head 3425 for scientific research outside atomic energy and space.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given by the Central Government to foreign governments are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 7601 - Loans and Advances to State Governments

e: Major Head 7605 is specifically assigned to Loans to Foreign Governments in the loans and advances group, distinct from 7601 loans to State Governments.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on urban development is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4215 - Capital Outlay on Water Supply and Sanitation
options.D: 4220 - Capital Outlay on Information and Publicity

e: Major Head 4217 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Urban Development, distinct from 4215 water supply and sanitation and 4216 housing.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for soil and water conservation are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6401 - Loans for Crop Husbandry
options.D: 6402 - Loans for Soil and Water Conservation

e: Loans heads mirror the function with a 6xxx code: Major Head 6402 is specifically assigned to Loans for Soil and Water Conservation.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for co-operation are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6425 - Loans for Co-operation
options.B: 6408 - Loans for Food Storage and Warehousing
options.D: 6515 - Loans for Other Rural Development Programmes

e: Major Head 6425 is specifically assigned to Loans for Co-operation in the agriculture and allied loans group of the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for rural development programmes other than those covered by the specific rural-development loan heads are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6425 - Loans for Co-operation
options.B: 6515 - Loans for Other Rural Development Programmes
options.C: 6402 - Loans for Soil and Water Conservation

e: Major Head 6515 is the residuary loans head for Other Rural Development Programmes, covering rural development loans not assigned to a specific head.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans and advances given by the Central Government to the Union Territory Governments are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 7601 - Loans and Advances to State Governments
options.C: 7602 - Loans and Advances to Union Territory Governments

e: Major Head 7602 is specifically assigned to Loans and Advances to Union Territory Governments, parallel to 7601 for State Governments.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the balances of the Sinking Funds are accounted for in the Public Account of India under Major Head:

options.A: 8011 - Insurance and Pension Funds

e: In the Public Account reserve funds group, Major Head 8222 is specifically assigned to Sinking Funds, created for amortisation and redemption of loans.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the civil advances, such as advances recoverable from Government servants and departments, are accounted for in the Public Account of India under Major Head:

options.A: 8550 - Civil Advances

e: Major Head 8550 is specifically assigned to Civil Advances in the Public Account, covering advances recoverable from government servants and departments.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the cash remittances and adjustments between officers rendering accounts to the same Accounts Officer are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 8675 - Deposits with Reserve Bank
options.B: 8782 - Cash Remittances and Adjustments between Officers Rendering Accounts to the Same Accounts Officer

e: Major Head 8782 covers Cash Remittances and Adjustments between Officers Rendering Accounts to the Same Accounts Officer, used for remittances within the same accounts circle.

q: In the classification of Railway accounts, the revenue expenditure on policy formulation, direction and other miscellaneous organisations of Indian Railways is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 3002 - Indian Railways - Working Expenses
options.C: 3001 - Indian Railways - Policy Formulation, Direction and Other Miscellaneous Organisation

e: Major Head 3001 is specifically assigned to Indian Railways - Policy Formulation, Direction and Other Miscellaneous Organisation in the railway revenue expenditure classification.

q: In the classification of accounts of the Union Government, the capital outlay on Indian Railways is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 3001 - Indian Railways - Policy Formulation, Direction and Other Miscellaneous Organisation
options.C: 5054 - Capital Outlay on Roads and Bridges

e: Major Head 5002 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Indian Railways in the Union Government accounts, distinct from railway working expenses heads 3002 and 3003.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Major Head 2701 from Major Head 4701 in the Government system of classification of accounts?

options.A: Major Head 2701 covers the revenue expenditure on medium irrigation, while Major Head 4701 covers the capital outlay on medium irrigation
options.B: Major Head 2701 covers the capital outlay on medium irrigation, while Major Head 4701 covers the revenue expenditure on medium irrigation
options.C: Major Head 2701 covers the revenue expenditure on minor irrigation, while Major Head 4701 covers the capital outlay on minor irrigation
options.D: Major Head 2701 is operated only by the Union Government, while Major Head 4701 is operated only by the State Governments

e: The first digit distinguishes revenue from capital for the same function: 2701 is revenue expenditure on Medium Irrigation and 4701 is Capital Outlay on Medium Irrigation.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Major Head 6001 from Major Head 6002 in the Government system of classification of accounts?

options.A: Major Head 6001 covers the external debt of the Central Government, while Major Head 6002 covers its internal debt
options.B: Major Head 6001 covers the internal debt of the Central Government, while Major Head 6002 covers its external debt
options.C: Major Head 6001 covers the internal debt of the State Governments, while Major Head 6002 covers the internal debt of the Central Government
options.D: Major Head 6001 is operated in the Public Account of India, while Major Head 6002 is operated in the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Major Head 6001 is Internal Debt of the Central Government and 6002 is External Debt of the Central Government, both in the Public Debt section of the Consolidated Fund.

q: The 'Revenue Deficit' of the Government for a year is:

options.A: The excess of its total expenditure over its total receipts for the year
options.B: The excess of its fiscal deficit over its capital expenditure for the year
options.C: The excess of its revenue expenditure over its revenue receipts for the year
options.D: The excess of its interest payments over its revenue receipts for the year

e: Revenue Deficit is by definition the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts; it shows the extent to which current expenditure is met from borrowings.

q: The 'Effective Revenue Deficit' of the Government for a year is arrived at by deducting, from the revenue deficit of that year:

options.A: The interest payments of the Government for the year
options.B: The capital expenditure of the Government for the year
options.C: The recoveries of loans and advances for the year
options.D: The grants given by the Government for the creation of capital assets

e: Effective Revenue Deficit is revenue deficit minus grants given for creation of capital assets, as those grants, though booked as revenue expenditure, create assets.

q: Wagner's law, relating to the growth of public expenditure, states that:

options.A: As the economy grows, the activities of the State, and with them public expenditure, tend to expand and increase in relative importance
options.B: Public expenditure rises in steps during a war or other social disturbance and does not return to its earlier level afterwards
options.C: Public expenditure should be carried to the point where its marginal social benefit equals the marginal social sacrifice of taxation
options.D: The burden of taxation should be so distributed that the aggregate sacrifice imposed is the least

e: Wagner's law of increasing State activity states that as an economy grows, State functions expand and public expenditure rises in relative importance.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'buoyancy' of a tax from its 'elasticity'?

options.A: Buoyancy measures the response of tax revenue to a change in the tax rate only, while elasticity measures its response to a change in the tax base only
options.B: Buoyancy measures the total response of tax revenue to growth in the tax base, including the effect of discretionary changes in rates and coverage, while elasticity measures only the automatic response of tax revenue to growth in the base, without any discretionary change
options.C: Buoyancy and elasticity are two names for one and the same response of tax revenue to growth in the base
options.D: Buoyancy applies only to direct taxes, while elasticity applies only to indirect taxes

e: Buoyancy includes the effect of discretionary rate and base changes in the total response of tax revenue to base growth, while elasticity measures only the automatic response with no discretionary change.

q: The canon of elasticity in taxation, added by writers later than Adam Smith, requires that:

options.A: The tax should be collected at the time and in the manner most convenient to the taxpayer
options.B: The cost of collecting the tax should be as small as possible in proportion to its yield
options.C: The system of taxation should be such that its yield can be increased or decreased according to the requirements of the State, and grows with the growth of the tax base
options.D: Every tax should be simple, plain and intelligible to the common taxpayer

e: The canon of elasticity, added after Adam Smith, requires a tax system whose yield can be raised or lowered as needed and grows automatically with growth of the tax base.

q: Zero-based budgeting, as a technique of budgeting, requires that:

options.A: Only a small incremental addition over the previous year's expenditure is provided for each programme in the Budget
options.B: Expenditure is linked to programmes and objectives, with a cost-benefit analysis of alternative ways of achieving them over a multi-year horizon
options.C: The Budget is balanced in every year, whatever the state of the economy
options.D: Every programme and item of expenditure is justified afresh from a zero base in each year's Budget, without assuming that the previous year's level of expenditure will continue

e: Zero-based budgeting requires every programme to be justified afresh from a zero base each year, with no assumption that the previous year's expenditure level will continue.

q: Indian Government Accounting Standard (IGAS) 1, formulated by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB), deals with:

options.A: Guarantees given by Governments - disclosure requirements
options.C: Loans and advances made by Governments

e: IGAS 1 issued by GASAB deals with Guarantees given by Governments - disclosure requirements, prescribing how guarantees are disclosed in government financial statements.

q: Indian Government Accounting Standard (IGAS) 3, formulated by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB), deals with:

options.A: Guarantees given by Governments - disclosure requirements
options.B: Loans and advances made by Governments
options.D: Cash flow statements of Government departments

e: IGAS 3 issued by GASAB deals with Loans and Advances made by Governments, prescribing their accounting, classification and disclosure.

q: The special procedure in respect of Money Bills, including the provision that a Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha, is laid down in the Constitution under:

options.A: Article 110

e: Article 109 of the Constitution lays down the special procedure for Money Bills, including that a Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha; Article 110 only defines a Money Bill.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on technical education is accounted for under Major Head 2202.
2. In the same system, the expenditure on sports and youth services is accounted for under Major Head 2205.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Technical education is under 2203, not 2202, and sports and youth services under 2204, not 2205, so both statements are wrong and the answer is neither.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Government system of classification of accounts, the civil advances are accounted for in the Public Account of India under Major Head 8550.
2. In the same system, the civil advances form part of the capital receipts of the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Statement 1 is correct: civil advances are under 8550 in the Public Account. Statement 2 is wrong, as Public Account advances are not capital receipts of the Consolidated Fund.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on major irrigation is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 2700 - Major Irrigation

e: Major Head 2700 is specifically assigned to Major Irrigation revenue expenditure, covering working expenses and maintenance of major irrigation projects.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on minor irrigation is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 2700 - Major Irrigation

e: Major Head 2702 is specifically assigned to Minor Irrigation revenue expenditure, distinct from 2700 major and 2701 medium irrigation.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on soil and water conservation is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4401 - Capital Outlay on Crop Husbandry
options.B: 4402 - Capital Outlay on Soil and Water Conservation
options.D: 4406 - Capital Outlay on Forestry and Wild Life

e: Major Head 4402 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Soil and Water Conservation, mirroring the corresponding revenue function in the agriculture group.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on fisheries is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4401 - Capital Outlay on Crop Husbandry

e: Major Head 4405 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Fisheries, distinct from 4401 crop husbandry, 4403 animal husbandry and 4404 dairy development.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on inland water transport is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 5056 - Capital Outlay on Inland Water Transport
options.C: 5054 - Capital Outlay on Roads and Bridges

e: Major Head 5056 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Inland Water Transport, mirroring revenue head 3056 in the transport capital group.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on transport services not covered by the specific transport capital heads is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 5053 - Capital Outlay on Civil Aviation
options.B: 5056 - Capital Outlay on Inland Water Transport
options.C: 5075 - Capital Outlay on Other Transport Services
options.D: 5051 - Capital Outlay on Ports and Light Houses

e: Major Head 5075 is the residuary head for Capital Outlay on Other Transport Services, covering transport services not assigned to a specific capital head.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on miscellaneous general services is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 5475 - Capital Outlay on Other General Economic Services
options.B: 4075 - Capital Outlay on Miscellaneous General Services
options.C: 5425 - Capital Outlay on Other Scientific Research
options.D: 5054 - Capital Outlay on Roads and Bridges

e: Major Head 4075 is specifically assigned to Capital Outlay on Miscellaneous General Services in the general services capital group.

q: In the accounts of a State Government, the internal debt of the State Government is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6001 - Internal Debt of the Central Government
options.B: 6002 - External Debt of the Central Government
options.C: 6004 - Loans and Advances from Central Government
options.D: 6003 - Internal Debt of the State Government

e: In State accounts, Major Head 6003 is Internal Debt of the State Government, parallel to 6001 for the Central Government, under the Public Debt section.

q: In the accounts of a State Government, the loans and advances received by it from the Central Government are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6004 - Loans and Advances from Central Government
options.B: 6003 - Internal Debt of the State Government
options.C: 6001 - Internal Debt of the Central Government
options.D: 7601 - Loans and Advances to State Governments

e: Major Head 6004 is specifically assigned to Loans and Advances from Central Government in State accounts, recording borrowings by the State from the Centre.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the balances of the General and Other Reserve Funds are accounted for in the Public Account of India under Major Head:

options.A: 8005 - State Reserve Funds

e: In the Public Account, Major Head 8121 is specifically assigned to General and Other Reserve Funds, distinct from provident funds and insurance and pension funds.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for housing are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6215 - Loans for Water Supply and Sanitation
options.D: 6202 - Loans for Education, Sports, Art and Culture

e: Major Head 6216 is specifically assigned to Loans for Housing in the social services loans group, distinct from 6215 water supply and sanitation and 6217 urban development.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for fisheries are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6401 - Loans for Crop Husbandry

e: Major Head 6405 is specifically assigned to Loans for Fisheries in the agriculture and allied loans group of the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for village and small industries are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 6851 - Loans for Village and Small Industries
options.D: 6853 - Loans for Non-ferrous Mining and Metallurgical Industries

e: Major Head 6851 is specifically assigned to Loans for Village and Small Industries, distinct from 6852 loans for industries generally.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the miscellaneous capital receipts of the Government, such as the receipts from disinvestment, are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 0075 - Miscellaneous General Services

e: Major Head 4000 is specifically assigned to Miscellaneous Capital Receipts, which include disinvestment receipts, in the capital receipts section of the Consolidated Fund.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts of the Government from miscellaneous general services, not covered by the specific receipt heads, are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 0070 - Other Administrative Services
options.C: 0071 - Contributions and Recoveries towards Pension and Other Retirement Benefits

e: Major Head 0075 is the residuary receipt head for Miscellaneous General Services, covering general services receipts not assigned to a specific head.

q: The Consolidated Fund of India and the Public Account of India are dealt with in the Constitution under:

options.A: Article 267

e: Article 266 of the Constitution deals with the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts of India and of the States, providing for credits to and withdrawals from them.

q: The Contingency Fund of India is established under the Constitution by:

options.A: Article 266

e: Article 267 of the Constitution provides for the Contingency Fund of India, placed at the disposal of the President for unforeseen expenditure pending parliamentary authorisation.

q: The constitutional provision that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law is contained in:

options.A: Article 265

e: Article 265 of the Constitution provides that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law, giving taxes their legal sanction requirement.

q: Supplementary, additional or excess grants, required where the amount authorised for a service is found insufficient or a need arises for expenditure on a new service during a financial year, are provided for in the Constitution under:

options.A: Article 112

e: Article 115 provides for supplementary, additional or excess grants when the authorised amount is insufficient or a new service arises during the financial year.

q: Votes on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants are provided for in the Constitution under:

options.A: Article 115

e: Article 116 provides for votes on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants, enabling the Lok Sabha to make grants in advance pending completion of the budget procedure.

q: The taxes and duties which are levied and collected by the Union but are shared between the Union and the States are dealt with in the Constitution under:

options.A: Article 268

e: Article 270 deals with taxes and duties levied and collected by the Union but shared between the Union and the States, forming the divisible pool.

q: The Goods and Services Tax Council is constituted under the Constitution by:

options.A: Article 279A

e: Article 279A, inserted by the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, constitutes the Goods and Services Tax Council to recommend on GST matters.

q: The Goods and Services Tax Council is chaired by:

options.A: The Prime Minister
options.D: The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India

e: Under Article 279A, the Goods and Services Tax Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, with State finance ministers as members.

q: A principal function of the Finance Commission is to make recommendations to the President as to:

options.A: The rate of dividend payable by Railways to General Finances
options.B: The distribution between the Union and the States of the net proceeds of taxes which are to be divided between them, and the allocation between the States of their respective shares
options.C: The quantum of borrowing to be raised by the Union Government in a year
options.D: The audit of the accounts of the Union and the States

e: A principal function of the Finance Commission under Article 280 is to recommend the distribution of net tax proceeds between the Union and States and the allocation of shares among States.

q: A tax levied on an activity which generates a negative externality, such as pollution, so as to make the private cost of the activity reflect its social cost, is known as:

options.A: A specific tax

e: A Pigouvian tax is levied on an activity generating a negative externality, like pollution, at a level that makes private cost reflect the social cost of the activity.

q: The Contingency Fund of a State, from which advances can be made to meet unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by the State Legislature, is placed at the disposal of:

options.A: The Governor of the State
options.B: The Finance Minister of the State
options.C: The Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly
options.D: The Accountant General of the State

e: The Contingency Fund of a State is placed at the disposal of the Governor under Article 267(2), to make advances for unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by the State Legislature.

q: Whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not is decided by:

options.A: The President of India
options.B: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha, whose decision in this respect is final

e: Under Article 110(3), if any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill, the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is final.

q: Re-appropriation of funds, as a budgetary device, is permissible:

options.A: Freely between two different grants, with the sanction of the Ministry of Finance
options.B: Only within the same grant, between its constituent units of appropriation, and not from one grant to another
options.C: From a charged appropriation to a voted grant, with the sanction of the Finance Commission
options.D: Between the grants of two different Ministries, with the sanction of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Re-appropriation is transfer of funds within the same grant from one unit of appropriation to another; transfer from one grant to another is not permissible as it would defeat parliamentary control.

q: The 'crowding out' effect in public finance refers to:

options.A: The displacement of State Government expenditure by Central Government expenditure in a federal set-up
options.B: The tendency of public expenditure to rise in steps during a war and not to return to its earlier level afterwards
options.C: The exclusion of small taxpayers from the tax net on account of a high exemption limit
options.D: The displacement of private investment because heavy Government borrowing in the capital market pushes up interest rates and leaves less finance for private borrowers

e: Crowding out occurs when heavy government borrowing raises interest rates in the capital market and leaves less finance for private borrowers, displacing private investment.

q: The 'Fiscal Deficit' of the Government for a year represents:

options.A: The excess of its total expenditure over its total receipts for the year, excluding borrowings and other liabilities
options.B: The excess of its revenue expenditure over its revenue receipts for the year
options.C: The excess of its interest payments over its revenue receipts for the year
options.D: The difference between its fiscal deficit and its interest payments for the year

e: Fiscal Deficit is total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings and other liabilities; it therefore shows the total borrowing requirement of government for the year.

q: A 'cess' levied by the Government is distinguished from an ordinary tax in that a cess is:

options.A: Levied only by the State Governments, and never by the Union Government
options.B: Always levied as a fixed amount per unit of the commodity taxed
options.C: Levied over and above a tax for a specific purpose, its proceeds being meant for that purpose
options.D: Shared compulsorily with the State Governments as part of the divisible pool of taxes

e: A cess is levied over and above a tax for a specific purpose and its proceeds are meant for that purpose, unlike a general tax whose proceeds go to general revenues.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes revenue receipts from capital receipts of the Government?

options.A: Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce an asset of the Government, while capital receipts either create a liability or reduce an asset
options.B: Revenue receipts are received only from taxation, while capital receipts are received only from non-tax sources
options.C: Revenue receipts require the vote of Parliament, while capital receipts do not form part of the Budget at all
options.D: There is no distinction, both being credited to the Public Account of India

e: Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce an asset, being current income, while capital receipts either create a liability, like borrowings, or reduce an asset, like disinvestment.

q: The classification of Government expenditure into 'plan' and 'non-plan' expenditure:

options.A: Continues to be the basis on which the Demands for Grants are presented to Parliament
options.B: Is required by the Constitution for the preparation of the Annual Financial Statement
options.C: Applies only to the expenditure of the State Governments
options.D: Has been dispensed with in the Union Budget, expenditure now being classified principally as revenue expenditure and capital expenditure

e: The plan and non-plan classification has been dispensed with in the Union Budget; expenditure is now classified principally as revenue expenditure and capital expenditure.

q: The 'Outcome Budget' presented by the Government primarily seeks to:

options.A: Compare the actual expenditure of a year with the grants voted by Parliament
options.B: Present the outlays provided for Ministries and Departments in terms of the deliverable outputs and outcomes expected to be achieved from them
options.C: Show the position of the public debt of the Government of India
options.D: Record the explanations for variations between actual expenditure and the final grant

e: The Outcome Budget presents outlays for Ministries and Departments in terms of deliverable outputs and outcomes expected from them, linking spending to results.

q: 'Performance budgeting', as a technique of budgeting, is primarily characterised by:

options.A: Budgeting strictly by the objects of expenditure, such as salaries and travel, without reference to the work to be done
options.B: Providing only a small incremental addition over the previous year's expenditure for each item
options.C: Presenting the Budget in terms of functions, programmes and activities, linking the money provided with the physical work and results to be achieved
options.D: Justifying every item of expenditure afresh from a zero base in each year

e: Performance budgeting presents the budget by functions, programmes and activities, linking money provided with the physical work and results to be achieved, not merely objects of expenditure.

q: The 'Gender Budget Statement', presented along with the Union Budget, primarily shows:

options.A: The salaries payable to women employees of the Government
options.B: Budgetary allocations for schemes and programmes that benefit women, in whole or in part
options.C: The receipts of the Government from taxes levied only on women
options.D: The allocations made to the Ministry of Women and Child Development alone

e: The Gender Budget Statement shows budgetary allocations for schemes and programmes that benefit women in whole or in part, not merely salaries of women employees.

q: The Economic Survey, presented to Parliament ahead of the Union Budget, is prepared under the guidance of:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: The Chief Economic Adviser in the Ministry of Finance

e: The Economic Survey is prepared in the Ministry of Finance under the guidance of the Chief Economic Adviser and is presented to Parliament ahead of the Union Budget.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an 'Interim Budget' from a 'Vote on Account'?

options.A: An Interim Budget is voted only by the Rajya Sabha, while a Vote on Account is voted only by the Lok Sabha
options.B: A Vote on Account is a complete Budget for the year, while an Interim Budget covers only a part of the year
options.C: There is no difference between the two, both being names for a grant made in advance of the regular Budget
options.D: An Interim Budget is a full statement of estimated receipts and expenditure for the year presented when a regular Budget cannot be passed in time, of which the Vote on Account, a grant in advance for a part of the year, forms a part

e: An Interim Budget is a full statement of estimated receipts and expenditure for the year presented when a regular Budget cannot be passed in time, and the Vote on Account for part of the year forms part of it.

q: The members of the Public Accounts Committee hold office for a term of:

options.A: Five years

e: Members of the Public Accounts Committee are elected for a term of one year, with re-election permitted, as per the Rules of Procedure of the Lok Sabha.

q: Along with the Annual Financial Statement, the statements required to be laid before Parliament under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management framework include:

options.A: The Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement, the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement and the Macro-economic Framework Statement
options.B: The Appropriation Accounts and the Finance Accounts of the previous year
options.C: The Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on the accounts of the Union
options.D: The Detailed Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways alone

e: Under the FRBM framework, the Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement, Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement and Macro-economic Framework Statement are laid before Parliament with the Annual Financial Statement.

q: 'Ways and Means Advances' extended by the Reserve Bank of India to the Government are intended to:

options.A: Finance the capital expenditure of the Government on long-term projects
options.B: Meet the dividend payable by Railways to General Finances
options.C: Replace the market borrowings of the Government altogether
options.D: Bridge temporary mismatches between the receipts and the payments of the Government

e: Ways and Means Advances from the Reserve Bank are short-term advances to bridge temporary mismatches between government receipts and payments, not to finance long-term projects.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. State Governments issue Treasury Bills of their own for their short-term borrowings.
2. Treasury Bills are issued by the Government of India to meet its short-term borrowing requirements.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only

e: Only statement 2 is correct: Treasury Bills are issued by the Government of India for short-term borrowing; State Governments do not issue Treasury Bills of their own.

q: The collections under the small savings schemes of the Government are credited to:

options.A: The Contingency Fund of India
options.B: The Consolidated Fund of India, as tax revenue
options.C: The National Small Savings Fund, maintained in the Public Account of India
options.D: The Depreciation Reserve Fund of Railways

e: Small savings collections are credited to the National Small Savings Fund maintained in the Public Account of India, from which they are on-lent, mainly to States.

q: Deposits held in the Public Account of India which remain unclaimed and lapse to the Government in accordance with the rules are credited to:

options.A: Government revenues, as a receipt of the Government
options.C: The Consolidated Sinking Fund of the State concerned
options.D: The personal accounts of the depositors' legal heirs in all cases

e: Deposits in the Public Account that remain unclaimed and lapse under the deposit rules are credited to government revenues as a receipt, under the lapsed deposits procedure.

q: In the classification of Railway capital expenditure, Plan Head 31 relates to:

options.A: New Lines

e: In the Railway Plan Head classification, Plan Head 31 relates to Track Renewals, covering renewal of rails, sleepers and fittings.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on co-operation is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 2425 - Co-operation

e: Major Head 2425 is specifically assigned to Co-operation revenue expenditure in the agriculture and allied group of the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on food storage and warehousing is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 2425 - Co-operation

e: Major Head 2408 is specifically assigned to Food Storage and Warehousing revenue expenditure, distinct from co-operation and other agricultural programmes.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on agricultural programmes not covered by the specific agricultural heads is accounted for under Major Head:

q: The principle of 'horizontal equity' in taxation requires that:

options.A: Persons in similar economic circumstances should be treated similarly for tax purposes, bearing a similar tax burden
options.B: Persons with a greater ability to pay should bear a proportionately greater tax burden than persons with a smaller ability to pay
options.C: Every person should pay exactly the same amount of tax, irrespective of his economic circumstances
options.D: The tax burden should fall only on persons who receive benefits from public expenditure

e: Horizontal equity requires persons in similar economic circumstances to be treated similarly and bear a similar tax burden; different treatment of equals would breach it.

q: 'Forward shifting' of a tax takes place when:

options.A: The taxpayer shifts the burden of the tax backwards to the supplier from whom he purchases his inputs
options.B: The taxpayer shifts the burden of the tax forwards to the buyer of his goods or services, through a higher price
options.C: The taxpayer bears the whole burden of the tax himself, without shifting it to any other person
options.D: The Government itself bears the burden of the tax by granting a subsidy to the taxpayer

e: Forward shifting occurs when the taxpayer passes the tax burden forwards to the buyer through a higher price of his goods or services, as with indirect taxes.

q: 'Tax capitalisation' in public finance refers to the process by which:

options.A: A tax is collected in advance from the taxpayer at the time of assessment
options.B: A tax is converted into a capital levy payable in instalments
options.C: The burden of a recurring tax on an asset is taken into account in reducing the price paid for the asset, so that the buyer is compensated for the future tax payments through the lower purchase price
options.D: The proceeds of a tax are credited to the capital account of the Government

e: Tax capitalisation occurs when a recurring tax on an asset is capitalised into a lower purchase price, so the buyer is compensated for future tax payments through paying less for the asset.

q: 'Demerit goods', in public finance, are goods:

options.A: Whose consumption the Government encourages and subsidises because their social benefit exceeds their private benefit
options.B: Which are supplied only by public sector undertakings
options.C: Which are exempted from taxation altogether
options.D: Whose consumption the Government discourages, through taxation or regulation, because it is regarded as harmful, such as tobacco and alcoholic liquor

e: Demerit goods are goods whose consumption government discourages through taxation or regulation because it is regarded as harmful, such as tobacco and alcoholic liquor.

q: The 'free-rider' problem, associated with public goods, arises because:

options.A: A person can enjoy the benefit of a public good without contributing to its cost, since he cannot be excluded from enjoying it once it is provided
options.B: The Government provides public goods free of charge to all citizens
options.C: Private producers refuse to supply goods to the Government at reasonable prices
options.D: Taxpayers are required to pay for public goods in advance of their provision

e: The free-rider problem arises because a public good is non-excludable: once provided, a person can enjoy its benefit without contributing to its cost.

q: 'Analytical procedures' (analytical review) in audit consist of:

options.A: Examining every voucher and supporting document relating to a transaction
options.B: Evaluating financial information through an analysis of plausible relationships among financial and non-financial data, and investigating fluctuations that are inconsistent with expectations
options.C: Physically verifying the assets held by the audited unit
options.D: Confirming balances directly with third parties in every case

e: Analytical procedures evaluate financial information by analysing plausible relationships among financial and non-financial data and investigating unexpected fluctuations, unlike vouching every transaction.
